newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Primakov says he hopes for successful NATO meeting.
newsitem.headline: Primakov says he hopes for successful NATO meeting.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov arrived in Luxembourg on Tuesday for key talks with NATO Secretary General Javier Solana on a new European security order and said he hoped for a successful result.
"I am hoping for a successful meeting," he told a group of waiting reporters at Luxembourg airport.
Solana and Primakov will meet at a secluded chateau outside the town centre at 7 p.m. (1700 gmt) for talks aimed at resolving the remaining obstacles to a new NATO-Russian charter.

The Western allies want the charter or "document", which gives Moscow a permanent consultative role with its old cold-war enemy, to form the centrepiece of a new security order in Europe and alleviate Russian concerns over the alliance's planned eastwards enlargement.
Moscow strongly opposes likely NATO membership for Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic and wants strong commitments from NATO setting clear limits on military activities in the new members.
NATO says such demands are out of the question because such issues are a matter of sovereignty.
